prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: receiving interface to outbound load release. Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork, trailer ID/seals, damage; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note on seal discrepancy); Pallet Dimension Scanner, alias Moonquarry (measures vs limits; produces Oversize Load Advisory, not placement authorization; supports oversize routing/handling); Inbound Pallet Buffer; North Aisle Stacker Crane, alias Juniperwake (sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot of occupied/available positions); South Aisle Stacker Crane; East/West Transfer Conveyors (vehicle-to-outbound-staging interfaces); Conveyor Line Controller, alias Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket per accepted induction); Autonomous Forklift Fleet, alias Larkspur (produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation after transfer: vehicle ID, pallet ID, time, incomplete/deferred moves); Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (validates arrivals vs receiving plan, flags unscheduled, directs to lane/door); Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment, applies authorized changes); Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk (shipment records from confirmed data); Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel (produces Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice on fire condition); Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, holds; reviews delays, vehicle stops, staging constraints before next wave); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authoritative task/inventory/priority state; releases work; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment on post-preparation destination/priority/sequence change; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; plans waves. Requirements: valid receipt instruction; window checked before door; seals/ID verified before unloading; damaged pallets segregated; unsafe issues pause unloading; restricted pallets in approved positions; cranes in authorized zones, valid targets; conveyor entry after inspection/ID; interlocks, presence sensors; blocked points hold upstream; single-pallet merges; duplicate inductions held; stale status holds; post-fault order preserved; no work without WMS release; sorter preserves committed order unless amendment authorizes, verifies staging vs plan before loading; forklifts accept work only with valid status/area/path, choose tasks by priority/battery/proximity, route considering access/readiness/pedestrians/restrictions, confirm pallet ID/location before lift, limit speed/turning, stop/reroute on safety blocks; work requests need unique task reference, destination, constraints; timely status avoids duplicate assignments.

New part:
S128: Yard Gate Controller records unresolved discrepancies for review and prevents an affected vehicle from proceeding when the discrepancy creates an operating risk.
S129: Yard Gate Controller uses the exception note to manage a receiving discrepancy at the gate.
S130: The receiving exception remains visible to the Warehouse Operations Supervisor until the discrepancy has been assessed and resolved.
S131: Inbound Inspection Desk records inspection outcomes before pallets enter routine warehouse handling.
S132: Inbound Pallet Buffer provides a controlled staging point when inspection or downstream handling is not yet ready.
S133: Pallet Dimension Scanner supplies measurements used to identify pallets that require a different handling path.
S134: Conveyor Line Controller coordinates conveyor movement and stops affected equipment when a downstream condition prevents safe transfer.
S135: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor provide separate routes for moving pallets between operating areas.
S136: Autonomous Forklift Fleet receives work only when a route and destination are available for the assigned vehicle.
S137: North Aisle Stacker Crane and South Aisle Stacker Crane report operating availability so task allocation can account for equipment status.
S138: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can defer work when a route conflict, equipment fault, or staging constraint remains unresolved.
S139: Maintenance Release Terminal is also known as Copperfield.
S140: Maintenance Release Terminal produces the Crane Service Release Card after required maintenance checks have been completed.
S141: Maintenance authorization is recorded before affected equipment is returned to operational service.
S142: Morrowglass reconciles work across operating areas and preserves a consistent view of task status and outstanding constraints.
S143: Outbound Dispatch Sorter organizes completed pallets according to the current shipping plan.
S144: Outbound Checkweigh Scale verifies shipment weight before the shipping record is finalized.
S145: Shipping Documentation Desk prepares shipment records from confirmed pallet and destination data.
S146: Fire Alarm Panel and Safety Zone Controller provide safety status that can require movement to stop or be restricted.
S147: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews delayed tasks, abnormal vehicle stops, and unresolved staging constraints before releasing the next outbound wave.
S148: Exception handling preserves a traceable hold state until the source of a discrepancy is understood and the affected pallet can be safely routed.
S149: A mismatch between expected and observed pallet attributes prevents automatic allocation and directs the load to controlled review.
S150: The operating record retains the scan result, location, and time of detection so that the review can be reconstructed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
